flagship.title: Under the laurels at Ivy Bluff
flagship.standfirst: Follow the Yadkin’s south bank on a short, rooty out-and-back with no obligation to cross a swollen creek.
flagship.why_this_week: At Ivy Bluff, mountain laurel and rhododendron frame the south bank of the Yadkin. The red circles lead over sloping ground and across creeks; 1.3 miles out is enough for a 2.6-mile return. Let Rupert sniff on a short leash away from the water’s edge. Turn before any crossing that looks slick or high, and skip the trip if the park posts a closure or the river is rising. Saturday has the better window in the dated forecast. Early Sunday showers are possible, so check the creek approaches and be ready to shorten the walk.

artwork.brief: Minimal close portrait after direct review of Plates 010–015 and reference 006. Recent run is mixed: woodland seat, waterside recline, navy play bow, standing meadow, olive seated look-back, fern-trail profile. This close portrait removes horizon and full-body silhouette, using frontal tilted listening head, cream paper and stronger expressive detail concentrated in the eyes, ears and collar. No destination or implied landmark. Distinct scale, posture, negative space and density from all recent full-body designs.

pivot.if: Thunder, unsafe footing, high water, strong winds or park closure
pivot.note: Postpone and recheck the official forecast and park status. Do not substitute an exposed outdoor outing.

conditions.trail_note: After rain, roots, rocks and creek approaches may be slick. Turn back before high or fast water or uncertain footing. Keep Rupert on a short leash away from the river’s edge.

practical.best_window: Favor late Saturday morning, after checking the latest forecast and park status. Allow up to two hours and return before dusk. Treat Sunday as conditional on safe footing and crossings after possible early showers.
practical.closures_note: Rechecked official park home, trail and news pages and reviewed the official river map. Ivy Bluff’s signed south-bank parking is at 4240 Shoals Road, East Bend, GPS 36.2537,-80.5087. No posted Ivy Bluff closure identified. November River Section hours 8:30 a.m.–6 p.m. The moderate hiking-only red-circle trail runs 1.3 miles each way across rooted slopes and creek crossings. Use an attended leash no longer than six feet and keep pets out of buildings. Stay clear of the riverbank and do not use the summit or the separate Bean Shoals access.
